from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite: The Individual vs. The Average", 
            [
                'Every population has a mean, labeled mu.', 
                'Standard deviation, sigma, measures the spread.', 
                'Individual data points are often messy and unpredictable.', 
                "Let's look at heights in a giraffe forest.", 
                'This raw distribution is chaotic and skewed.'
            ]
        )
        
        # Elements to be grouped later
        forest_elements = VGroup()

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Horizontal Axis
        axis = Line(self.grid['D1'], self.grid['D6'], color=WHITE)
        axis_label = Text("Height", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        axis_label.next_to(axis, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        # Mean Line
        mu_pos = self.grid['D2'] + RIGHT * 0.5
        mean_line = Line(mu_pos + DOWN * 0.5, mu_pos + UP * 2.0, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        
        # μ label using Unicode
        mu_label = Text("μ", color=WHITE, font_size=30)
        mu_label.next_to(mean_line, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(axis), Write(axis_label))
        self.play(Create(mean_line), Write(mu_label))
        
        forest_elements.add(axis, axis_label, mean_line, mu_label)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#ADD8E6"))
        
        # Sigma indicator (spread range)
        sigma_line = DoubleArrow(
            mu_pos + UP * 0.5, 
            mu_pos + RIGHT * 1.2 + UP * 0.5, 
            buff=0, color="#ADD8E6", tip_length=0.1
        )
        
        # σ label using Unicode
        sigma_label = Text("σ", color="#ADD8E6", font_size=30)
        sigma_label.next_to(sigma_line, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(sigma_line), Write(sigma_label))
        forest_elements.add(sigma_line, sigma_label)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#ADD8E6"))
        
        # Scatter 100 circles (messy population)
        np.random.seed(42)
        points = VGroup()
        for _ in range(100):
            # Skewed x position using log-normal distribution
            rel_x = np.random.lognormal(mean=0.3, sigma=0.4)
            # Map log-normal values to grid space
            x_coord = self.grid['D1'][0] + rel_x * 0.8
            # Scatter y randomly above the axis
            y_coord = self.grid['D1'][1] + np.random.uniform(0.2, 2.5)
            
            # Clamp x to stay within the axis bounds
            x_coord = min(max(x_coord, self.grid['D1'][0]), self.grid['D6'][0])
            
            dot = Dot(point=[x_coord, y_coord, 0], radius=0.04, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.6)
            points.add(dot)

        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(p) for p in points], lag_ratio=0.02), run_time=2)
        forest_elements.add(points)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#90EE90"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        # Simple skewed curve representation
        skewed_curve = VGroup()
        curve_points = [
            self.grid['D1'] + UP*0.2,
            self.grid['D2'] + UP*2.2,
            self.grid['D3'] + UP*1.2,
            self.grid['D4'] + UP*0.6,
            self.grid['D5'] + UP*0.3,
            self.grid['D6'] + UP*0.2
        ]
        curve = VMobject(color=YELLOW).set_points_as_corners(curve_points).make_smooth()
        self.play(Create(curve))
        forest_elements.add(curve)
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial layout setup
        lines = [
            'Instead of everyone, we take a random sample.',
            'This sample has a specific size, called n.',
            'We calculate the average for this small group.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Sampling Experiment", lines)

        # --- Scene Preparation ---
        # Number lines for population and sampling distribution
        # label_constructor=Text is added to avoid the FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        top_axis = NumberLine(
            x_range=[0, 10, 1], 
            length=5, 
            include_numbers=True, 
            font_size=16, 
            color=WHITE,
            label_constructor=Text
        )
        bottom_axis = NumberLine(
            x_range=[0, 10, 1], 
            length=5, 
            include_numbers=True, 
            font_size=16, 
            color=WHITE,
            label_constructor=Text
        )
        
        self.place_in_area(top_axis, 'B1', 'B6')
        self.place_in_area(bottom_axis, 'F1', 'F6')
        
        # Labels for axes
        pop_label = Text("Population Heights", font_size=14).next_to(top_axis, UP, buff=0.2)
        dist_label = Text("Sample Means Distribution", font_size=14).next_to(bottom_axis, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        # Population generation (static dots)
        np.random.seed(42)
        population_vals = np.random.normal(5, 1.2, 100)
        population_vals = np.clip(population_vals, 0.5, 9.5)
        pop_dots = VGroup(*[
            Dot(top_axis.n2p(v) + UP * np.random.uniform(0.1, 0.4), radius=0.03, color="#888888") 
            for v in population_vals
        ])

        self.add(top_axis, bottom_axis, pop_label, dist_label, pop_dots)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight sample
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        sample_indices = np.random.choice(range(100), 30, replace=False)
        sample_dots = VGroup(*[pop_dots[i] for i in sample_indices])
        
        self.play(
            sample_dots.animate.set_color("#00FF00").scale(1.5),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display sample size n
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        n_label = Text("n = 30", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(n_label, 'C3')
        
        self.play(Write(n_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Calculation and dropping points
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        calc_box = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=1.8, height=0.6, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(calc_box, 'D3')
        calc_text = Text("Calculate Average", font_size=14).move_to(calc_box.get_center())
        calculation_group = VGroup(calc_box, calc_text)
        
        self.play(Create(calculation_group))
        
        # Animation: Sample dots move to calculator, then drop one yellow dot
        sample_copy = sample_dots.copy()
        current_mean = np.mean([population_vals[i] for i in sample_indices])
        mean_dot = Dot(bottom_axis.n2p(current_mean), color="#FFFF00", radius=0.08)
        
        self.play(
            sample_copy.animate.move_to(calc_box.get_center()).scale(0.1).set_opacity(0),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            TransformFromCopy(calc_box, mean_dot),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Repeat sampling 10 times quickly
        fast_means = VGroup(mean_dot)
        for _ in range(9):
            new_indices = np.random.choice(range(100), 30, replace=False)
            new_mean = np.mean([population_vals[i] for i in new_indices])
            new_dot = Dot(bottom_axis.n2p(new_mean), color="#FFFF00", radius=0.06)
            
            # Fast highlight and drop
            temp_sample = VGroup(*[pop_dots[i] for i in new_indices])
            self.play(
                temp_sample.animate(run_time=0.15).set_color("#00FF00"),
                FadeIn(new_dot, run_time=0.15),
                rate_func=linear
            )
            self.play(temp_sample.animate(run_time=0.1).set_color("#888888"), rate_func=linear)
            fast_means.add(new_dot)

        # Final "Rain" of 1,000 dots (simulated with 150 for performance)
        rain_dots = VGroup()
        for _ in range(150):
            # Simulated sample means according to CLT (narrower distribution)
            m = np.mean(np.random.choice(population_vals, 30))
            # Add small random jitter in y for visual density
            jitter_y = np.random.uniform(0, 0.5)
            d = Dot(bottom_axis.n2p(m) + UP * jitter_y, color="#FFFF00", radius=0.04, fill_opacity=0.7)
            rain_dots.add(d)
        
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(
                *[FadeIn(d) for d in rain_dots],
                lag_ratio=0.015,
                run_time=3
            )
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial layout setup
        lecture_lines = [
            'We repeat this sampling process many, many times.',
            'Watch as thousands of sample averages are plotted.',
            'A specific shape begins to emerge from the chaos.',
            'Despite the messy start, we see a bell curve.',
            'This is the magic of the sampling distribution.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Transformation (The 'Magic' Moment)", lecture_lines)

        # Define Colors
        DOT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        BELL_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        MEAN_COLOR = "#00FFFF"
        MESSY_COLOR = "#FFA500"
        LABEL_COLOR = "#FFD700"

        # Setup Axes for the simulation
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[0, 1, 0.2],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": GRAY}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Normal Distribution Curve for Line 3 onwards
        def gaussian(x):
            return np.exp(-x**2 / 1.0) * 0.8
        
        bell_curve = axes.plot(gaussian, color=BELL_COLOR, stroke_width=4)
        
        # Messy Curve for Line 4 comparison
        def messy_distribution(x):
            return (0.3 * np.exp(-(x+1.5)**2 / 0.5) + 0.5 * np.exp(-(x-1.0)**2 / 0.8)) * 0.7
        
        messy_curve = axes.plot(messy_distribution, color=MESSY_COLOR, stroke_width=3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line 1 is active (White is default)
        sample_indicator = Text("Sampling...", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(sample_indicator, "B3")
        self.play(Write(sample_indicator))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(sample_indicator))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(DOT_COLOR)
        self.add(axes)

        # Animation: Dots stacking (Simulating thousands)
        num_dots = 100 
        dots = VGroup()
        bins = {i: 0 for i in np.arange(-3, 3.1, 0.2)}
        
        for _ in range(num_dots):
            val = np.random.normal(0, 0.7)
            closest_bin = min(bins.keys(), key=lambda x: abs(x - val))
            bins[closest_bin] += 0.05
            dot = Dot(point=axes.c2p(closest_bin, bins[closest_bin]), radius=0.04, color=DOT_COLOR)
            dots.add(dot)

        self.play(LaggedStart(*(Create(d) for d in dots), lag_ratio=0.015, run_time=3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(MEAN_COLOR)

        # Transition dots to curve
        self.play(FadeOut(dots), Create(bell_curve), run_time=1.5)

        # Vertical line of symmetry
        mean_line = axes.get_vertical_line(axes.c2p(0, gaussian(0)), color=MEAN_COLOR, line_func=DashedLine)
        mean_label = Text("Mean of Averages", font_size=16, color=MEAN_COLOR)
        # Positioning label near the top of the line
        label_pos = axes.c2p(0, 0.9)
        mean_label.move_to(label_pos + UP * 0.3)

        self.play(Create(mean_line), Write(mean_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(MESSY_COLOR)

        messy_label = Text("Original Shape", font_size=16, color=MESSY_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(messy_label, "B1", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(messy_curve), Write(messy_label))
        self.play(Indicate(messy_curve, color=MESSY_COLOR), Indicate(bell_curve, color=BELL_COLOR))
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(messy_curve), FadeOut(messy_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(LABEL_COLOR)

        normal_label = Text("Normal Distribution", font_size=24, color=LABEL_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(normal_label, "C5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(normal_label))
        self.play(normal_label.animate.scale(1.1), run_time=0.5, rate_func=there_and_back)
        self.wait(2)

        # Reset colors for final state
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the basic layout
        title = "The Core Rules of CLT"
        lines = [
            "The curve's center matches the true population mean.",
            "Larger samples create a narrower, more precise curve.",
            "Usually, thirty or more samples ensure this symmetry."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Helper function for Normal Distribution curve
        def normal_pdf(x, mu, sigma):
            return (1 / (sigma * np.sqrt(2 * np.pi))) * np.exp(-0.5 * ((x - mu) / sigma)**2)

        # Setup Axes in the animation area (B2 to E5)
        # We'll use a range of -4 to 4 on x, and 0 to 1.5 on y
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 1.2, 0.5],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": WHITE},
            tips=False
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), run_time=0.5)

        # Baseline curve (moderate sigma)
        curve_base = axes.plot(lambda x: normal_pdf(x, 0, 0.8), color=WHITE, x_range=[-4, 4])
        
        # Dashed line and Mean label
        peak_x = 0
        peak_y = normal_pdf(peak_x, 0, 0.8)
        dashed_line = DashedLine(
            start=axes.c2p(peak_x, peak_y),
            end=axes.c2p(peak_x, 0),
            color=WHITE
        )
        mu_label = Text("μ", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(mu_label, "F4", scale_factor=0.8)
        # Adjust mu_label to be just below the axis
        mu_label.next_to(axes.c2p(0, 0), DOWN, buff=0.2)

        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve_base))
        self.play(Create(dashed_line), Write(mu_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight second line
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#32CD32"), run_time=0.5)

        # Define Wide curve (n=5 -> larger sigma) and Narrow curve (n=50 -> smaller sigma)
        # Note: We keep mu at 0 to show center consistency
        # sigma_wide ~ 1.0, sigma_narrow ~ 0.35
        curve_wide = axes.plot(lambda x: normal_pdf(x, 0, 1.0), color="#FF6347", x_range=[-4, 4])
        curve_narrow = axes.plot(lambda x: normal_pdf(x, 0, 0.35), color="#32CD32", x_range=[-4, 4])
        
        label_n5 = Text("n = 5", font_size=20, color="#FF6347")
        label_n50 = Text("n = 50", font_size=20, color="#32CD32")
        
        # Position labels near the curves
        self.place_at_grid(label_n5, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_n50, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Transition: Remove base curve, add the two comparison curves
        self.play(
            FadeOut(curve_base),
            Create(curve_wide),
            Create(curve_narrow),
            Write(label_n5),
            Write(label_n50)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight third line
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"), run_time=0.5)

        # Magic Threshold Text
        threshold_text = Text("Magic Threshold: n ≥ 30", color="#FFD700", weight=BOLD)
        self.place_in_area(threshold_text, "A2", "A5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Add highlight or box for the threshold text
        surround_rect = SurroundingRectangle(threshold_text, color="#FFD700", buff=0.2)

        self.play(Write(threshold_text))
        self.play(Create(surround_rect))
        self.wait(2)

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # Animation sequence

            Create(axes),
            Create(curve),
            FadeOut(sampling_box, sampling_text, belt, belt_label),
            run_time=2

        # Dot representing an average falling onto the curve
        avg_dot = Dot(color=WHITE).move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        self.play(avg_dot.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0.8)), run_time=1)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(failure_zone_left),
            FadeIn(failure_zone_right),
            Write(fail_label)
        )
        
        self.wait(3)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            'We moved from messy data to orderly curves.', 
            'The CLT is the bridge to powerful statistics.', 
            'Understand the average to master the whole.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Conclusion", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight Line 1
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#ADD8E6"))
        
        # Create a cloud of chaotic dots in area A1 to B6
        dots = VGroup()
        colors = ["#ADD8E6", "#FFA500"]
        for _ in range(50):
            dot = Dot(radius=0.05, color=np.random.choice(colors))
            # Random position within top area (A1 to B6)
            x_rand = np.random.uniform(0.5, 5.5)
            y_rand = np.random.uniform(1.2, 2.2)
            dot.move_to([x_rand, y_rand, 0])
            dots.add(dot)
            
        # Create funnel lines
        funnel_left = Line(self.grid["C1"], self.grid["D3"], color=WHITE)
        funnel_right = Line(self.grid["C6"], self.grid["D4"], color=WHITE)
        funnel = VGroup(funnel_left, funnel_right)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dots), Create(funnel))
        
        # Funneling animation: dots converge to the funnel neck
        neck_point = (self.grid["D3"] + self.grid["D4"]) / 2
        self.play(
            dots.animate.scale(0.1).move_to(neck_point),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=exponential_decay
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight Line 2
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700")
        )
        
        # Emerging Bell Curve in area E1 to F6
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[0, 0.5],
            x_length=4, y_length=2,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "include_ticks": False, "color": GREY_C}
        )
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: np.exp(-x**2 / 2) / np.sqrt(2 * np.pi), color="#FFD700")
        bell_curve_group = VGroup(axes, curve)
        self.place_in_area(bell_curve_group, "E1", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Glowing effect (simulated by a slightly larger, semi-transparent copy)
        glow = curve.copy().set_stroke(width=8, opacity=0.3)
        bell_curve_glow = VGroup(bell_curve_group, glow)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(bell_curve_glow, shift=DOWN),
            dots.animate.set_opacity(0),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight Line 3
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF")
        )
        
        # Final concluding text
        conclusion_text = Text("The Bridge to Statistical Power", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")
        # Place it between the funnel neck and the bell curve
        self.place_in_area(conclusion_text, "D1", "D6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(conclusion_text))
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Magic of Averages: Understanding the Central Limit Theorem
outline.target_audience: University students or introductory data science learners

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Individual vs. The Average
sections.content: Introduce the basic building blocks: Population Mean (μ) and Standard Deviation (σ). Explain that individual data points in a population can be messy and unpredictable, but their average follows a different rule.
sections.example: Imagine a 'Forest of Giraffes.' Some are very short (calves), and some are extremely tall. If we graph all their heights, the shape is chaotic and skewed, not a neat bell curve. We label the average height as μ.

sections.title: The Sampling Experiment
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'Sampling.' Instead of looking at every giraffe, we take a random group (a sample) of size 'n' and calculate their specific average.
sections.example: A drone flies over the forest and randomly picks 30 giraffes. It calculates their average height and drops a single data point onto a new graph. We repeat this 'sampling' process 1,000 times.

sections.title: The Transformation (The 'Magic' Moment)
sections.content: Visualizing the 'Sampling Distribution of the Sample Mean.' As we plot more and more sample averages, a specific shape begins to emerge regardless of the original population's shape.
sections.example: An animation shows thousands of dots falling. Even though the original forest height chart was lopsided, the chart of the *averages* starts piling up in the center, forming a perfect, symmetrical Bell Curve (Normal Distribution).

sections.title: The Core Rules of CLT
sections.content: Define the three mathematical pillars of the Central Limit Theorem: 1. The center of the bell is the population mean (μ). 2. The curve gets narrower as sample size (n) increases. 3. The magic threshold is usually n ≥ 30.
sections.example: Show a side-by-side comparison: A sample size of n=5 creates a fat, wide bell. A sample size of n=50 creates a skinny, tall needle-like bell, showing that larger samples give us more certainty about the true average.

sections.title: Why It Matters: Real-World Application
sections.content: Explain that CLT allows us to make confident predictions about a whole population even when we don't know its distribution, as long as we have samples.
sections.example: A chocolate factory (The 'Cocoa-Bot 3000') produces bars. Each bar's weight varies slightly and unpredictably. By weighing batches of 40 bars (sampling), the manager can use the CLT Bell Curve to predict exactly how often the machinery will fail or produce underweight snacks.

sections.title: Summary & Conclusion
sections.content: Recap the journey from 'Messy Population' to 'Orderly Bell Curve.' Emphasize that CLT is the bridge between simple descriptions and powerful statistical inference.
sections.example: A final graphic shows a chaotic cloud of dots (the population) being funneled through a 'Sample Filter' and emerging as a glowing, golden Bell Curve at the bottom.

Standard deviation, sigma, measures the spread.
Individual data points are often messy and unpredictable.

This raw distribution is chaotic and skewed.

lecture_lines: First, we select a random sample of thirty giraffes.
Next, we calculate the average height for this group.
This average becomes a single dot on our graph.
We repeat this process multiple times to gather data.
Watch as a thousand sample averages rain down below.

Watch as thousands of sample averages are plotted.
A specific shape begins to emerge from the chaos.
Despite the messy start, we see a bell curve.
This is the magic of the sampling distribution.

storyboard.title: The Core Rules of CLT
lecture_lines: The curve's center matches the true population mean.
Larger samples create a narrower, more precise curve.
Usually, thirty or more samples ensure this symmetry.
